questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+10{x}_{3}=-8 \\  & {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=-8-10{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}=6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8-10{x}_{3} \\ 6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=2 \\  & y+2z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-z=2 \\  & y+2z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+z \\ y=-2z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the latter can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2+z \\ -2z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y+z=0 \\  & -4x+6y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system is consistent dependent
- The system has no solution
- The system is consistent independent
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 6 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 6 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we can to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement I is true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+3y=-1 \\  & x-2y=1 \\  & -x-5y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- The system has no solution
- The system is consistent independent
- The system is consistent dependent
questions.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 \\ -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=1 \\ 7y=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=-\frac{3}{7}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-\frac{3}{7})=1\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{7}.
$$

 
So, we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

questions.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+4y=2 \\  & 2x+(k+1)y=3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k+1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k+1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & k-7 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4y=2 \\ (k-7)y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=7,$ then the second equation is $0=-1,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=7.$

questions.problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x+2y=12 \\  & x+ky=4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 12 \\ 1 & k & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & k & 4 \\ 0 & 2-3k & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+ky=4 \\  & (2-3k)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=\frac{2}{3},$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x+ky=4.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=\frac{2}{3}.$

Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-2y=1, \\ 4x+ky=-3\end{aligned}

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
We can use Gaussian elimination to find the general solutions of systems with any number of equations and variables. For instance, consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1, \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This system has the augmented matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14121479/assets/8a8452587098eed9b697c3999c356359b949429f29ce16af2c81cf728be9480e.svg)

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\, & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable $z.$ From the second equation, we get $y=-3z,$ and from the first equation, we obtain $x=1-4z.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-4z, \\ y=-3z, \\ z=z.\end{aligned}
$$

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-4z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
We can use Gaussian elimination to find the general solutions of systems with any number of equations and variables. For instance, consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1, \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

This system has the augmented matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14121479/assets/8a8452587098eed9b697c3999c356359b949429f29ce16af2c81cf728be9480e.svg)

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\, & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+4z=1 \\ y+3z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable $z.$ From the second equation, we get $y=-3z,$ and from the first equation, we obtain $x=1-4z.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-4z, \\ y=-3z, \\ z=z.\end{aligned}
$$

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-4z \\ -3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Consistent and Inconsistent Systems of Linear Equations
tutorials.problem:
Recall that a system of linear equations is called **consistent** if it has at least one solution. Otherwise, if there are no solutions, the system is called **inconsistent**. 

For a consistent system, 

- the system is called **consistent independent** if the solution is unique, while

- the system is called **consistent dependent** if there are infinitely many solutions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14121479/assets/f5b808eac6e1d865b13b68ce2a4f7d317560ae3965928e478531fcd2148c2c6b.png)
